propositions: Extraction from free-text LLM replies is heuristic and vulnerable to schema-valid decoys winning over intended content; an explicit marker channel makes payload location a contract instead of inference.

The implementation extends schema_directive to wrap single final JSON objects between literal line-anchored markers (<<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>> and <<<END>>>) and refactors parse_structured to iterate complete marker blocks in reverse order, returning the first validated block or raising fail-closed if none validate.
Markerless replies (no complete marker block found) fall back byte-for-byte to today's schema-filtered selection pipeline, ensuring df3a-era and non-compliant-model transcripts are unaffected.

Marker pairing is line-anchored and non-nested: each <<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>> pairs with the next <<<END>>> in document order; repeated/interleaved markers follow left-to-right next-close semantics (OPEN...OPEN...END yields one block; OPEN...END...OPEN...END yields two blocks with last-block-wins).

The bounded-retry prompt in structured_run.py is updated to name the markers so the fail-closed retry channel matches the first attempt, and test_provider_parity.py is re-derived to single-source the entire directive string rather than assuming the schema is trailing.

AC5 live measurement (run 31003041092) confirms per-cell parse-success non-regression versus a40f baseline (anthropic +6/20, bedrock +2/20, openai −1/20 via markerless path) with material improvement on channel-driven (fenced) cells, though live marker adoption under the proxy was 0/20.
